newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish reinsurance firm PTR to boost capital in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Polish reinsurance firm PTR to boost capital in Q2.

text.p: Poland's first reinsurer Polskie Towarzystwo Reasekuracyjne SA (PTR) plans to boost its capital to at least 100 million zlotys from the current 65 million by issuing new shares in the second quarter, PTR's president said.
Krzysztof Jarmuszczak told Reuters in an interview on Monday new shares would be earmarked for Polish insurance firms and also for passive investors from outside the sector, both Polish and foreign.
"We want to have a capital of at least 100 million zlotys this year... The issue will be in the second quarter of 1997," he said.
Jarmuszczak said current shareholders could increase their stakes in the firm, but said none of the firms should have more than 12.5 percent stake in the raised capital.

PTR shareholders include state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), its subsidary PZU Life, state-owned Bank Handlowy SA, Polish copper concern KGHM SA and the state treasury -- each holding 19.18 percent stakes.
Industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim and TUiR Warta insurer have 1.92-percent stakes each. Polisa and PTU Energo-Asekuracja insurers hold the remaining shares.
Jarmuszczak said that the firm would like to increase its capital to about $50 million in the next four or five years.
He also said PTR would like to enter the Warsaw Stock Exchange, possibly in 2000. "Entering the bourse is a part of the firm's development strategy," he said.

Jarmuszczak said that during four months of 1996 following the firm's launch in September, PTR collected premiums worthy 400,000 zlotys. This year it expected to collect about 50 million zlotys in premiums. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
